lines:
Responsibilities: Owns Chat-scoped job identity and lifecycle for every asynchronous capability producer. A job's runner is either a supervised OS process session (shell, shell_start, python, python_start) or a delegated background child Agent run (tool.subagent, tool.subagent_fork, tool.subagent_message); the kind is registry data, not a second scheduler. It owns durable start intents and observations, running and terminal snapshots, bounded output cursors and collection acknowledgement, retained-work disposition, capacity, keep/stop/input/list control routing, and the completion gate a final assistant answer must pass.

Owned state: one JobRecord per job with kind (process or subagent), owner Chat, invoking Agent/child scope, model-facing label, running/terminal snapshot, captured-output byte counts and cursor, collected/kept/interrupted disposition, and - for a child job - the delegated child identity and its terminal outcome. Child live progress (one line per model turn) and the child's own job inventory are registry facts; the child's conversation and evidence remain the child scope's and are never merged into the parent transcript.

Contracts: the durable broker authorizes each control (job_output, job_input, job_stop, job_keep, job_list) and the registry settles it. job_output returns status, bounded cursor output and, for a child job, kind=subagent with its durable childId, live progress and terminal outcome; job_input steers a running child at its next step boundary or resumes a settled child as a new background turn-set, and sends stdin to a process; job_stop cancels the runner and closes a child scope so it can never be resumed; job_keep records deliberate retention so the delegating Agent may finish while the work continues; completion_notice_scoped reports unresolved running or uncollected jobs to the Agent loop.

Invariants: jobs never cross Chat boundaries, and a control is additionally scoped to the exact delegating Agent/child where one applies. Identity is committed before the side effect, and a terminal state is committed before it can be observed as collected. Process runners retain complete descendant-tree control; child runners use the child's own cancellation token and stop the child-scoped jobs they still own. Capacity bounds live and retained jobs (8 per Chat, 32 total) and a refused start is an explicit typed failure rather than a silent drop.

Failure and recovery: restart marks every running job interrupted, releases retention, and never replays it; a process tree cannot be reconstructed from a PID and a child is not re-run. A child job's committed frame is then reported interrupted rather than running, and a continuation starts a fresh turn-set from the child's committed head. Collection is acknowledged only after the broker durably records the returned output, so a crash before that boundary leaves it readable again.

Performance and NFRs: one supervisor pass drives runner snapshots and persistence; output is read by cursor from captured logs instead of buffered in memory; a kind index serves control lookups; bounded job history is evicted oldest-first only when terminal and collected; no job control requires a project.

Non-responsibilities: no capability authorization or approval decision (Invocation Broker), no OS process spawning, health or descendant-tree mechanics (Process-Tree Supervisor), no graph scheduling or Agent-loop execution (Workflow Runtime Worker), no canonical semantic history, and no secret materialization.

data.name: Chat Job Registry & Completion Barrier
data.technology: Rust owner-scoped job registry over supervised process and delegated-child runners
